download_if_not_local <- function(url, dest) {
  dest_path <- file.path("data_raw", dest)
  if (!file.exists(dest_path)) {
    message("Downloading ", dest)
    download.file(url, dest_path, mode = "wb")
  } else {
    message(dest, " already exists, skipping.")
  }
}

replace_nuance <- function(df, nuances_mapping) {
  for (nuance_i in seq_along(nuances_mapping)) {
    for (liste_noms in nuances_mapping[nuance_i]) {
      for (nom in liste_noms) {
        df[df==nom] <- names(nuances_mapping)[nuance_i]
      }
    }
  }
  df
}

#-------------------------------
# Helper function: long table into wide table (proportions)
#
make_wide <- function(df, label) {
  df |>
    dplyr::group_by(bureau, nuance) |>
    dplyr::summarise(votes = sum(votes, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::group_by(bureau) |>
    dplyr::mutate(pct = votes / sum(votes)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::select(bureau, nuance, pct) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = nuance, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0) |>
    dplyr::rename_with(~ paste0(label, "_", .), -bureau) |>
    dplyr::select(where(~ !all(. == 0)))
}

# Ensure all wide tables have the full set of 5 political bloc columns
ensure_nuances <- function(wide_df, prefix) {
  nuances <- c("extreme_gauche", "gauche", "centre", "droite", "extreme_droite")
  expected_cols <- paste0(prefix, "_", nuances)
  for (col in expected_cols) {
    if (!col %in% names(wide_df)) {
      message("Adding missing column: ", col)
      wide_df[[col]] <- 0
    }
  }
  wide_df
}

#prepare for cca
to_share_matrix <- function(wide_df) {
  # Remove duplicate bureaux before converting to matrix
  wide_df <- wide_df |> dplyr::distinct(bureau, .keep_all = TRUE)
  mat <- wide_df |>
    dplyr::select(-bureau) |>
    as.matrix()
  rownames(mat) <- wide_df$bureau
  mat
}

# Extract numeric matrix (remove bureau column)
X <- all_elections_clean |>
  dplyr::select(-bureau) |>
  as.matrix()

# ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Run PCA
# center = TRUE  :  subtract column mean (centering)
# scale. = TRUE  :  divide by SD (scaling)
#                 
pca <- prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)

# Check variance explained by each principal component
importance <- summary(pca)$importance
cat("Variance explained by each PC:\n")
print(round(importance[, 1:6] * 100, 1))  #show first 6

# Plot 1: Scree Plot 

variance_df <- data.frame(
  PC       = paste0("PC", 1:length(pca$sdev)),
  variance = (pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100,  # convert to %
  cumvar   = cumsum((pca$sdev^2) / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100)  # cumulative
) |> slice(1:6)  #  show first 6

ggplot(variance_df, aes(x = reorder(PC, -variance), y = variance)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4E79A7", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(group = 1), color = "#E15759", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#E15759", size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = cumvar, group = 1), color = "#76B7B2",
            linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 80, color = "grey50", linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("text", x = 8, y = 82, label = "80% cumulative variance",
           size = 3, color = "grey50") +
  labs(
    title    = " Scree Plot —Lyon Elections PCA",
    subtitle = "Blue bars = variance per PC | Red = variance | Dashed = cumulative",
    x        = " Principal Component",
    y        = "Variance Explained (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
#meaning of PC1-PC2

#scree_per_election

# Plot 2: Compare PC1 variance explained across elections
# This answers: which election had the most political polarization?
run_pca_single <- function(wide_df, tag) {
  mat <- wide_df |>
    dplyr::select(-bureau) |>
    as.matrix()
  
  pca_res <- prcomp(mat, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)
  imp <- summary(pca_res)$importance
  
  list(
    pca    = pca_res,
    bureaux = wide_df$bureau,
    pc1    = round(imp[2, 1] * 100, 1),   # PC1  %
    pc2    = round(imp[2, 2] * 100, 1),   # PC2  %
    tag    = tag
  )
}

pca_eu14    <- run_pca_single(w_eu14,    "EU 2014")
pca_p17r1   <- run_pca_single(w_p17r1,   "Pres 2017 R1")
pca_leg17r1 <- run_pca_single(w_leg17r1, "Leg 2017 R1")
pca_mun20r1 <- run_pca_single(w_mun20r1, "Mun 2020 R1")
pca_p22r1   <- run_pca_single(w_p22r1,   "Pres 2022 R1")

variance_compare <- data.frame(
  election = c("EU 2014", "Pres 2017\nR1", "Leg 2017\nR1",
               "Mun 2020\nR1", "Pres 2022\nR1"),
  pc1 = c(pca_eu14$pc1, pca_p17r1$pc1, pca_leg17r1$pc1,
           pca_mun20r1$pc1, pca_p22r1$pc1),
  pc2 = c(pca_eu14$pc2, pca_p17r1$pc2, pca_leg17r1$pc2,
           pca_mun20r1$pc2, pca_p22r1$pc2)
) |>
  mutate(total = pc1 + pc2,
         election = factor(election, levels = election))

# Convert to long format for stacked bars
variance_long <- variance_compare |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(pc1, pc2),
               names_to = "component",
               values_to = "variance") |>
  mutate(component = ifelse(component == "pc1", "PC1", "PC2"))

ggplot(variance_long, aes(x = election, y = variance, fill = component)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.85, width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    data = variance_compare,
    aes(x = election, y = total + 1.5,
        label = paste0(total, "%")),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("PC1" = "#4E79A7", "PC2" = "#A0C4E2"),
                    name = " Component") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 70, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = 71.5,
           label = "70% Reference", size = 3, color = "grey50", hjust = 0) +
  labs(
    title    = " PC1+PC2 Variance Explained per Election",
    subtitle = "Higher = political divide more concentrated on left-right axis",
    x = "", y = " Variance Explained (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Plot 3: Correlation circles for all elections (2×3 grid)
# Check if variable directions are consistent across elections

make_circle_data <- function(pca_result, label) {
  as.data.frame(pca_result$pca$rotation[, 1:2]) |>
    rownames_to_column("variable") |>
    mutate(
      election = label,
      length   = sqrt(PC1^2 + PC2^2),
      nuance   = case_when(
        str_detect(variable, "extreme_gauche") ~ "Ext.gauche",
        str_detect(variable, "gauche")         ~ "Gauche",
        str_detect(variable, "centre")         ~ "Centre",
        str_detect(variable, "droite") & !str_detect(variable, "extreme") ~ "Droite",
        str_detect(variable, "extreme_droite") ~ "Ext.droite",
        TRUE ~ "Divers"
      )
    )
}

# PLOT 4/5/6/7— Biplots (one per election, 5 total)

make_biplot <- function(pca_result, wide_df, title, filename) {

  imp     <- summary(pca_result$pca)$importance
  pc1_pct <- round(imp[2, 1] * 100, 1)
  pc2_pct <- round(imp[2, 2] * 100, 1)

  # Station scores
  scores <- as.data.frame(pca_result$pca$x[, 1:2]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(bureau = pca_result$bureaux)

  #  Scale loadings to match score range
  scale_factor <- max(abs(scores[, 1:2])) /
    max(abs(pca_result$pca$rotation[, 1:2])) * 0.65

  loadings <- as.data.frame(pca_result$pca$rotation[, 1:2]) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      PC1s   = PC1 * scale_factor,
      PC2s   = PC2 * scale_factor,
      nuance = dplyr::case_when(
        stringr::str_detect(variable, "extreme_gauche") ~ "Ext.gauche",
        stringr::str_detect(variable, "gauche") &
          !stringr::str_detect(variable, "extreme") ~ "Gauche",
        stringr::str_detect(variable, "centre")         ~ "Centre",
        stringr::str_detect(variable, "droite") &
          !stringr::str_detect(variable, "extreme") ~ "Droite",
        stringr::str_detect(variable, "extreme_droite") ~ "Ext.droite",
        TRUE ~ "Divers"
      ),
      length = sqrt(PC1^2 + PC2^2)
    ) |>
    dplyr::group_by(nuance) |>
    dplyr::slice_max(order_by = length, n = 2) |>
    dplyr::ungroup()

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey80", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey80", linetype = "dashed") +
    # Station points (blue dots)
    geom_point(data  = scores,
               aes(x = PC1, y = PC2),
               alpha = 0.3, color = "steelblue", size = 1.8) +
    #  Extreme station labels
    geom_text_repel(
      data = scores |> dplyr::filter(
        abs(PC1) > quantile(abs(PC1), 0.93) |
        abs(PC2) > quantile(abs(PC2), 0.93)
      ),
      aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, label = bureau),
      size = 2.5, color = "steelblue",
      alpha = 0.8, max.overlaps = 15
    ) +
    # Political nuance arrows
    geom_segment(data = loadings,
                 aes(x = 0, y = 0,
                     xend = PC1s, yend = PC2s,
                     color = nuance),
                 arrow     = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm")),
                 linewidth = 1.1, alpha = 0.9) +
    # Arrow labels
    geom_text_repel(data = loadings,
                    aes(x = PC1s, y = PC2s,
                        label = variable, color = nuance),
                    size = 3.2, fontface = "bold",
                    max.overlaps = 30, show.legend = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, name = "Nuance") +
    labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = paste0(
        "Blue dots = polling stations | Arrows = political nuances | ",
        "PC1: ", pc1_pct, "% | PC2: ", pc2_pct, "%"
      ),
      x = paste0("PC1 (", pc1_pct, "%)"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", pc2_pct, "%)")
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15),
          legend.position = "right")

  print(p)
 # ggsave(paste0("figures/", filename, ".png"),
 #        plot = p, width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 150)
  #cat(filename, "\n")
}

# ============================================================
#  II. CCA — CANONICAL CORRELATION ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

run_cca <- function(m1, m2, tag1, tag2) {
  
  tag <- paste0(tag1, "_vs_", tag2)
  
  # Step 1: find common stations and align row order
  common_ids <- intersect(rownames(m1), rownames(m2))
  m1 <- m1[match(common_ids, rownames(m1)), , drop = FALSE]
  m2 <- m2[match(common_ids, rownames(m2)), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(m1) <- common_ids
  rownames(m2) <- common_ids
  message("CCA ", tag, ": ", length(common_ids), " common polling stations")

  # Step 2: drop last column to remove linear dependency (shares sum to 1)
  m1_cca <- m1[, -ncol(m1), drop = FALSE]
  m2_cca <- m2[, -ncol(m2), drop = FALSE]

  # Step 3: filter zero-variance and NA/Inf columns for cancor() only
  keep1 <- apply(m1_cca, 2, function(x)
    !any(is.na(x) | is.nan(x) | is.infinite(x)) && var(x) > 0)
  keep2 <- apply(m2_cca, 2, function(x)
    !any(is.na(x) | is.nan(x) | is.infinite(x)) && var(x) > 0)
  m1_cca <- m1_cca[, keep1, drop = FALSE]
  m2_cca <- m2_cca[, keep2, drop = FALSE]

  message("  m1 valid columns (", ncol(m1_cca), "): ",
          paste(colnames(m1_cca), collapse = ", "))
  message("  m2 valid columns (", ncol(m2_cca), "): ",
          paste(colnames(m2_cca), collapse = ", "))

  # Step 4: skip if either matrix has 0 columns
  if (ncol(m1_cca) == 0 || ncol(m2_cca) == 0) {
    warning("CCA ", tag, " skipped: no valid columns after filtering.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }

  # Step 5: run CCA
  cca <- stats::cancor(m1_cca, m2_cca)

  # Align coefficient directions for interpretability
  for (d in seq_along(cca$cor)) {
    f <- sign(sum(cca$xcoef[, d] * cca$ycoef[, d]))
    cca$xcoef[, d] <- cca$xcoef[, d] * f
    cca$ycoef[, d] <- cca$ycoef[, d] * f
  }

  # Step 6: compute canonical scores using filtered matrices
  n_can <- min(2, ncol(cca$xcoef), ncol(cca$ycoef))
  U <- m1_cca %*% cca$xcoef[, seq_len(n_can), drop = FALSE]
  V <- m2_cca %*% cca$ycoef[, seq_len(n_can), drop = FALSE]

  # Step 7: correlate full matrices with canonical scores (all blocs shown in plot)
  cor_mat1 <- cor(m1, U)
  colnames(cor_mat1) <- paste0("dim", seq_len(n_can))
  cor_mat2 <- cor(m2, V)
  colnames(cor_mat2) <- paste0("dim", seq_len(n_can))

  # If only one canonical dimension, add dim2 = 0 so ggplot can render
  if (!"dim2" %in% colnames(cor_mat1)) {
    cor_mat1 <- cbind(cor_mat1, dim2 = 0)
    cor_mat2 <- cbind(cor_mat2, dim2 = 0)
  }

  df_plot <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    as.data.frame(cor_mat1) |>
      tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") |>
      dplyr::mutate(election = tag1),
    as.data.frame(cor_mat2) |>
      tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") |>
      dplyr::mutate(election = tag2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    nuance_raw = stringr::str_remove(variable, "^[^_]+_"),
    nuance = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "extreme_gauche")                      ~ "Ext.gauche",
      stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "gauche") &
        !stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "extreme")                          ~ "Gauche",
      stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "centre")                              ~ "Centre",
      stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "droite") &
        !stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "extreme")                          ~ "Droite",
      stringr::str_detect(nuance_raw, "extreme_droite")                      ~ "Ext.droite",
      TRUE                                                                   ~ "Divers"
    )
  )

  circle <- tibble::tibble(
    x = cos(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 300)),
    y = sin(seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 300))
  )

  color_palette <- c(
    "Ext.gauche" = "#B22222", "Gauche" = "#E15759",
    "Centre"     = "#F28E2B", "Droite" = "#4E79A7",
    "Ext.droite" = "#1a1a6e", "Divers" = "#76B7B2"
  )

#Plot 9/10/11/12/13: CCA correlation circle plot  
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    df_plot, ggplot2::aes(x = dim1, y = dim2, colour = nuance)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_path(
      data = circle,
      ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y),
      colour = "grey70", inherit.aes = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
      ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = dim1, yend = dim2),
      arrow = ggplot2::arrow(length = ggplot2::unit(0.15, "cm")),
      linewidth = 0.8
    ) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
      ggplot2::aes(label = variable),
      size = 3.5, fontface = "bold",
      max.overlaps = 20, show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ election) +
    ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, name = "Nuance") +
    ggplot2::coord_fixed(xlim = c(-1.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.05)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = paste0("CCA — ", tag),
      subtitle = paste0(
        "r1 = ", round(cca$cor[1], 3),
        " | r2 = ", round(cca$cor[2], 3)
      ),
      x = paste0("Canonical dim 1  (r = ", round(cca$cor[1], 3), ")"),
      y = paste0("Canonical dim 2  (r = ", round(cca$cor[2], 3), ")")
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  print(p)

  message("CCA done: ", tag,
          " | r1 = ", round(cca$cor[1], 3),
          " | r2 = ", round(cca$cor[2], 3))

  invisible(list(cca = cca, plot = p, n_stations = length(common_ids)))
}

# RUN CCA — 5 comparisons selected for research relevance
# ============================================================

# IV. Clustering
# ============================================================
# Goal: group polling stations by voting behaviour
# Input: combined share matrix from the most recent elections
# Methods: K-means (multiple k + initializations) +
#          Hierarchical (multiple distances + linkage methods)

# ---- Build combined feature matrix for clustering ----
# Use p17r1, mun20r1, p22r1 — most informative and closest to leg2024
common_bureaux <- Reduce(intersect, list(
  rownames(sm_p17r1),
  rownames(sm_mun20r1),
  rownames(sm_p22r1)
))

X_cluster <- cbind(
  sm_p17r1[common_bureaux, ],
  sm_mun20r1[common_bureaux, ],
  sm_p22r1[common_bureaux, ]
)
cat("Clustering matrix:", nrow(X_cluster), "stations x", ncol(X_cluster), "variables\n")

# PLOT 14 — Silhouette Analysis
sil_scores <- sapply(2:7, function(k) {
  set.seed(42)
  km  <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  sil <- cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(X_cluster))
  mean(sil[, 3])
})

sil_df <- tibble::tibble(k = 2:7, silhouette = sil_scores)
best_k  <- sil_df$k[which.max(sil_df$silhouette)]
cat("Optimal k by silhouette:", best_k, "\n")

ggplot2::ggplot(sil_df, ggplot2::aes(x = k, y = silhouette)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(colour = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = best_k,
                      colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
  ggplot2::annotate("text", x = best_k + 0.15, y = max(sil_scores) - 0.005,
                    label = paste0("best k = ", best_k),
                    colour = "red", hjust = 0) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Silhouette analysis — optimal number of clusters",
    x = "Number of clusters k",
    y = "Mean silhouette width (higher = better)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

# K-MEANS CLUSTERING
set.seed(42)
km_k2 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = 2,      nstart = 25)
km_k3 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = 3,      nstart = 25)
km_k4 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = best_k, nstart = 25)
km_k5 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = 5,      nstart = 25)

# Compare different random initializations at optimal k
set.seed(1);  km_init1 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = best_k, nstart = 1)
set.seed(99); km_init2 <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = best_k, nstart = 1)
set.seed(42); km_best  <- kmeans(X_cluster, centers = best_k, nstart = 25)

cat("ARI: single init 1 vs best (nstart=25):",
    round(mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_init1$cluster, km_best$cluster), 3), "\n")
cat("ARI: single init 2 vs best (nstart=25):",
    round(mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_init2$cluster, km_best$cluster), 3), "\n")
# High ARI = kmeans result is stable regardless of initialization

pca_cluster <- prcomp(X_cluster, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)


#PLOT 15/16 — K-means Clusters on PCA Plane (2 plots: k=2, k=3)
plot_kmeans_pca <- function(km_result, pca_res, title) {
  df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(km_result$cluster,
                                   labels = paste0("C", seq_len(max(km_result$cluster)))))
  imp <- summary(pca_res)$importance
  ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = cluster)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.5) +
    ggplot2::stat_ellipse(level = 0.80, linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = "Ellipses show 80% confidence regions per cluster",
      x = paste0("PC1 (", round(imp[2,1]*100, 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", round(imp[2,2]*100, 1), "%)"),
      colour = "Cluster"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}

plot_kmeans_pca(km_k2,  pca_cluster, paste0("K-means k=2 on PCA plane"))
plot_kmeans_pca(km_k3,  pca_cluster, paste0("K-means k=3 on PCA plane"))

## PLOT17 — Cluster Political Profile (heatmap)
plot_cluster_profile <- function(km_result, title) {
  BLOCS <- c("extreme_gauche", "gauche", "centre", "droite", "extreme_droite")

  # Average share per cluster, only using p22r1 columns for readability
  cols_p22 <- colnames(X_cluster)[grepl("p22r1", colnames(X_cluster))]

  profile <- as.data.frame(X_cluster[, cols_p22]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(km_result$cluster,
                                   labels = paste0("Cluster ", seq_len(max(km_result$cluster))))) |>
    dplyr::group_by(cluster) |>
    dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), mean), .groups = "drop") |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-cluster, names_to = "bloc", values_to = "share") |>
    dplyr::mutate(bloc = stringr::str_remove(bloc, "^p22r1_"),
                  bloc = factor(bloc, levels = c(
                    "extreme_gauche", "gauche", "centre",
                    "droite", "extreme_droite")))

  ggplot2::ggplot(profile, ggplot2::aes(x = bloc, y = cluster, fill = share)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = scales::percent(share, accuracy = 0.1)),
                       size = 3.5) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7fbff", high = "#2171b5",
                                  labels = scales::percent_format()) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = title,
      x     = "Political bloc (left → right)",
      y     = "Cluster",
      fill  = "Mean share (Pres 2022 R1)"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
}

plot_cluster_profile(km_k4, paste0("Cluster profiles — k=", best_k))

# ---- Hierarchical clustering: compare distances and linkage methods ----
run_hclust <- function(dist_method, link_method, k, tag) {
  d  <- dist(X_cluster, method = dist_method)
  hc <- hclust(d, method = link_method)
  clusters <- cutree(hc, k = k)

  # Plot dendrogram
  plot(hc, labels = FALSE,
       main = paste0("Dendrogram — dist=", dist_method,
                     " | link=", link_method, " | k=", k),
       xlab = "", sub = "")
  rect.hclust(hc, k = k, border = "red")

  message("HClust done: dist=", dist_method,
          " | link=", link_method, " | k=", k,
          " | tag=", tag)
  invisible(clusters)
}

# Test 4 combinations as required
hc_ward      <- run_hclust("euclidean", "ward.D2",  best_k, "ward")
hc_complete  <- run_hclust("euclidean", "complete", best_k, "complete")
hc_average   <- run_hclust("euclidean", "average",  best_k, "average")
hc_manhattan <- run_hclust("manhattan", "ward.D2",  best_k, "manhattan_ward")

# ---- ARI comparison: all methods against each other ----
ari_results <- tibble::tibble(
  comparison = c(
    "kmeans vs hclust ward",
    "kmeans vs hclust complete",
    "kmeans vs hclust average",
    "kmeans vs hclust manhattan+ward",
    "hclust ward vs complete",
    "hclust ward vs average",
    "hclust ward vs manhattan+ward"
  ),
  ARI = round(c(
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_k4$cluster,  hc_ward),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_k4$cluster,  hc_complete),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_k4$cluster,  hc_average),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(km_k4$cluster,  hc_manhattan),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(hc_ward,         hc_complete),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(hc_ward,         hc_average),
    mclust::adjustedRandIndex(hc_ward,         hc_manhattan)
  ), 3),
  interpretation = dplyr::case_when(
    ARI > 0.8 ~ "Very similar",
    ARI > 0.6 ~ "Similar",
    ARI > 0.4 ~ "Moderate",
    TRUE      ~ "Weak"
  )
)
print(ari_results)

#Project hierarchical clustering results onto 
# the PCA plane
# ============================================================

plot_hclust_pca <- function(hclust_vector, pca_res, title) {
  # hclust_vector is the integer vector returned by cutree(), e.g., hc_ward
  
  df <- as.data.frame(pca_res$x[, 1:2]) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cluster = factor(hclust_vector,
                                   labels = paste0("C", seq_len(max(hclust_vector)))))
  imp <- summary(pca_res)$importance
  
  ggplot2::ggplot(df, ggplot2::aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, colour = cluster)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.5) +
    ggplot2::stat_ellipse(level = 0.80, linewidth = 0.8) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = title,
      subtitle = "Ellipses show 80% confidence regions per cluster",
      x = paste0("PC1 (", round(imp[2,1]*100, 1), "%)"),
      y = paste0("PC2 (", round(imp[2,2]*100, 1), "%)"),
      colour = "Cluster"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}

# ============================================================
# PLOTTING: Compare the distributions of the 4 hierarchical 
# clustering methods on the PCA plane
# ============================================================

# Plot Ward method results (Euclidean distance)
p_ward <- plot_hclust_pca(hc_ward, pca_cluster, "Hierarchical (Euclidean + Ward) on PCA plane")
print(p_ward)

# Plot Complete linkage method results (Euclidean distance)
p_complete <- plot_hclust_pca(hc_complete, pca_cluster, "Hierarchical (Euclidean + Complete) on PCA plane")
print(p_complete)

# Plot Average linkage method results (Euclidean distance)
p_average <- plot_hclust_pca(hc_average, pca_cluster, "Hierarchical (Euclidean + Average) on PCA plane")
print(p_average)

# Plot Ward method results (Manhattan distance)
p_manhattan <- plot_hclust_pca(hc_manhattan, pca_cluster, "Hierarchical (Manhattan + Ward) on PCA plane")
print(p_manhattan)

#
# ============================================================
# V. REGRESSION — Download, clean, and prepare 2024 data
# ============================================================

# ---- Load new datasets ----
euro2024_raw   <- read.csv("data_raw/euro2024.csv",   sep = ";", encoding = "UTF-8")
leg2024_r1_raw <- read.csv("data_raw/leg2024_r1.csv", sep = ";", encoding = "UTF-8")

# ---- Filter Lyon only (code commune = 69123) ----
euro2024_lyon    <- euro2024_raw   |> dplyr::filter(Code.commune == 69123)
leg2024_r1_lyon  <- leg2024_r1_raw |> dplyr::filter(Code.commune == 69123)

cat("Euro 2024 Lyon bureaux:", nrow(euro2024_lyon), "\n")
cat("Leg 2024 R1 Lyon bureaux:", nrow(leg2024_r1_lyon), "\n")

# ---- Inspect nuance codes ----
# Euro 2024: nuances are in Nuance.liste.1, Nuance.liste.2, ...
euro_nuances <- euro2024_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.liste\\.")) |>
  unlist() |> unique() |> sort()
cat("Euro 2024 nuances:\n"); print(euro_nuances)

# Leg 2024: nuances are in Nuance.candidat.1, Nuance.candidat.2, ...
leg_nuances <- leg2024_r1_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.candidat\\.")) |>
  unlist() |> unique() |> sort()
cat("Leg 2024 R1 nuances:\n"); print(leg_nuances)


# ---- pivot_wider → long 的結構（確認nuance後補完）----

# Euro 2024: pivot Nuance.liste.N + Voix.N → long format
euro2024_long <- euro2024_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(Code.BV,
                dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.liste\\.\\d+$"),
                dplyr::matches("^Voix\\.\\d+$")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Code.BV,
    names_to  = c(".value", "num"),
    names_pattern = "^(Nuance\\.liste|Voix)\\.(\\d+)$"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Nuance.liste), Voix > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bureau = stringr::str_pad(as.character(Code.BV), 4, "left", "0"),
    nuance = Nuance.liste,
    votes  = Voix
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(bureau, nuance, votes)

# Leg 2024 R1: same structure but column names differ
leg2024_r1_long <- leg2024_r1_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(Code.BV,
                dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.candidat\\.\\d+$"),
                dplyr::matches("^Voix\\.\\d+$")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = -Code.BV,
    names_to  = c(".value", "num"),
    names_pattern = "^(Nuance\\.candidat|Voix)\\.(\\d+)$"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Nuance.candidat), Voix > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bureau = stringr::str_pad(as.character(Code.BV), 4, "left", "0"),
    nuance = Nuance.candidat,
    votes  = Voix
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(bureau, nuance, votes)

# ---- Nuance mapping for Euro 2024 ----
# Source: https://www.resultats-elections.interieur.gouv.fr
nuances_mapping_euro2024 <- list(
  extreme_gauche = list("LEXG", "LFI", "LCOM"),
  gauche         = list("LDVG", "LUG", "LVEC", "LECO"),
  centre         = list("LENS", "LREC"),
  droite         = list("LDVD", "LLR"),
  extreme_droite = list("LEXD", "LRN"),
  divers         = list("LDIV")
)

# ---- Nuance mapping for Leg 2024 R1 ----
nuances_mapping_leg2024 <- list(
  extreme_gauche = list("EXG"),
  gauche         = list("UG", "ECO"),
  centre         = list("ENS", "UDI", "REC"),
  droite         = list("LR"),
  extreme_droite = list("RN"),
  divers         = list("DIV")
)

# ---- Pivot Euro 2024 to long format ----
euro2024_long <- euro2024_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(Code.BV,
                dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.liste\\.\\d+$"),
                dplyr::matches("^Voix\\.\\d+$")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols         = -Code.BV,
    names_to     = c(".value", "num"),
    names_pattern = "^(Nuance\\.liste|Voix)\\.(\\d+)$"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Nuance.liste), Voix > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bureau = stringr::str_pad(as.character(Code.BV), 4, "left", "0"),
    nuance = Nuance.liste,
    votes  = Voix
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(bureau, nuance, votes) |>
  replace_nuance(nuances_mapping_euro2024)

# ---- Pivot Leg 2024 R1 to long format ----
leg2024_r1_long <- leg2024_r1_lyon |>
  dplyr::select(Code.BV,
                dplyr::matches("^Nuance\\.candidat\\.\\d+$"),
                dplyr::matches("^Voix\\.\\d+$")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols         = -Code.BV,
    names_to     = c(".value", "num"),
    names_pattern = "^(Nuance\\.candidat|Voix)\\.(\\d+)$"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Nuance.candidat), Nuance.candidat != "", Voix > 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    bureau = stringr::str_pad(as.character(Code.BV), 4, "left", "0"),
    nuance = Nuance.candidat,
    votes  = Voix
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(bureau, nuance, votes) |>
  replace_nuance(nuances_mapping_leg2024)

# ---- Convert to wide share tables ----
w_euro2024   <- make_wide(euro2024_long,   "euro2024")
w_leg2024_r1 <- make_wide(leg2024_r1_long, "leg2024")

w_euro2024   <- ensure_nuances(w_euro2024,   "euro2024")
w_leg2024_r1 <- ensure_nuances(w_leg2024_r1, "leg2024")

cat("Euro 2024 bureaux:", nrow(w_euro2024), "\n")
cat("Leg 2024 R1 bureaux:", nrow(w_leg2024_r1), "\n")

# ---- Build regression dataset ----
# Join all explanatory variables + response variable on bureau ID
# Use only round 1 elections as explanatory variables
reg_data <- w_leg2024_r1 |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_eu14,    by = "bureau") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_p17r1,   by = "bureau") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_leg17r1, by = "bureau") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_mun20r1, by = "bureau") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_p22r1,   by = "bureau") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(w_euro2024, by = "bureau") |>
  # Add cluster label from k-means as a categorical explanatory variable
  dplyr::left_join(
    tibble::tibble(
      bureau  = names(km_k4$cluster),
      cluster = factor(km_k4$cluster, labels = paste0("C", seq_len(max(km_k4$cluster))))
    ),
    by = "bureau"
  ) |>
  na.omit()

cat("Regression dataset:", nrow(reg_data), "polling stations\n")
cat("Variables:", ncol(reg_data), "\n")

# ============================================================
# Run one linear regression per political bloc
# Y = leg2024 bloc share
# X = same bloc share across all past elections + cluster
# ============================================================

blocs <- c("extreme_gauche", "gauche", "centre", "droite", "extreme_droite")

run_bloc_regression <- function(bloc, data) {

  y_col <- paste0("leg2024_", bloc)

  # Explanatory variables: same bloc from each past election + cluster
  x_cols <- c(
    paste0("eu14_",     bloc),
    paste0("p17r1_",    bloc),
    paste0("leg17r1_",  bloc),
    paste0("mun20r1_",  bloc),
    paste0("p22r1_",    bloc),
    paste0("euro2024_", bloc),
    "cluster"
  )

  # Keep only columns that exist in the data
  x_cols <- x_cols[x_cols %in% colnames(data)]

  formula <- as.formula(paste(y_col, "~", paste(x_cols, collapse = " + ")))
  model   <- lm(formula, data = data)

  list(bloc = bloc, model = model, summary = summary(model))
}

# Run all 5 models
reg_models <- lapply(blocs, run_bloc_regression, data = reg_data)
names(reg_models) <- blocs

# ============================================================
# PLOT: Regression results summary
# R² per bloc + coefficient plot
# ============================================================

# ---- Table: R² and key statistics per bloc ----
reg_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  bloc    = blocs,
  r2      = sapply(reg_models, function(m) round(summary(m$model)$r.squared, 3)),
  adj_r2  = sapply(reg_models, function(m) round(summary(m$model)$adj.r.squared, 3)),
  p_value = sapply(reg_models, function(m) {
    f <- summary(m$model)$fstatistic
    round(pf(f[1], f[2], f[3], lower.tail = FALSE), 4)
  })
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    fit_quality = dplyr::case_when(
      r2 > 0.8 ~ "Excellent",
      r2 > 0.6 ~ "Good",
      r2 > 0.4 ~ "Moderate",
      TRUE     ~ "Weak"
    )
  )

print(reg_summary)

# ---- Plot 1: R² comparison across blocs ----
ggplot2::ggplot(reg_summary,
                ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(bloc, r2), y = r2, fill = fit_quality)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(width = 0.6, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = paste0("R²=", r2)),
                     hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
  values = c("Excellent" = "#2E5F8A", "Good"     = "#5B8DB8",
             "Moderate"  = "#A0BDD4", "Weak"     = "#6B7F8E"),
  name = "Fit quality"
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip(ylim = c(0, 1.05)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title    = "Regression R² per Political Bloc",
    subtitle = "Response: Leg 2024 R1 | Explanatory: elections 2014–2024 + cluster",
    x        = "Political bloc",
    y        = "R² (proportion of variance explained)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
theme(plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "grey40"),
      legend.position  = "right",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

# ---- Plot 2: Coefficient plot for each bloc ----
# 

plot_coefficients <- function(reg_model_item) {

  coef_df <- broom::tidy(reg_model_item$model, conf.int = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      significant = p.value < 0.05,
      term        = stringr::str_remove(term, "cluster")
    )

  ggplot2::ggplot(coef_df,
                  ggplot2::aes(x = reorder(term, estimate),
                               y = estimate,
                               colour = significant)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    ggplot2::geom_pointrange(
      ggplot2::aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
      linewidth = 0.8, size = 0.6
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
      values = c("TRUE" = "#4E79A7", "FALSE" = "grey70"),
      labels = c("TRUE" = "p < 0.05", "FALSE" = "p ≥ 0.05"),
      name   = "Significance"
    ) +
    ggplot2::coord_flip() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title    = paste0("Coefficients — ", reg_model_item$bloc),
      subtitle = paste0("R² = ", round(summary(reg_model_item$model)$r.squared, 3)),
      x        = "",
      y        = "Coefficient (95% CI)"
    ) +
   ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
ggplot2::theme(plot.title       = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold"),
               plot.subtitle    = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "grey40"),
               legend.position  = "right",
               panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank())
}

# Install broom if needed
if (!requireNamespace("broom", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("broom")
library(broom)

# Generate one coefficient plot per bloc
lapply(reg_models, plot_coefficients) |> invisible()

# ---- Print full model summaries ----
for (bloc in blocs) {
  cat("\n", rep("=", 60), "\n")
  cat("MODEL:", bloc, "\n")
  cat(rep("=", 60), "\n")
  print(summary(reg_models[[bloc]]$model))
}
